chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruvetkalam (திருவேட்களம்): in one the poet vows never to forget the vision of Murugan's feet, faces and gracious look that ended his impurity; in the other he confesses chasing gold for women and praising fools as gods, and asks whether he must wander so.
structure_note: 747 is a song of remembrance with no confession; 748 confesses wasted life and begging.

747.reading: The poet vows he will not forget what Murugan showed him: the experience of Siva's grace, the anklet feet that dried up his anava impurity, the twelve shoulders and six faces, the form on the peacock that showed the sea of compassion, and the look that gently brought him among the devotees of three Tamils so that he might reach the supreme state. The praise names the vel that scattered the mountains and the Suras' crowns, the goddess who is the power of the foot that struck Death, and Vishnu who set Vidura against Duryodhana and drove Arjuna's chariot, at Thiruvetkalam.
747.nuance: Each line ends in a thing seen (பாதம், கோலம், பார்வை) and the whole song hangs on மறவேனே, 'I will not forget': it is thanksgiving, not plea. ஆணவ மலம் அற்றிட is Saiva Siddhanta language for the root impurity. சிவபத்தினி கூற்றினை மோதிய பதசத்தினி makes the goddess the power in the foot that kicked Death, the left foot being hers. The opening lines (சதுரத்தரை நோக்கிய பூவொடு கதிரொத்திட ஆக்கிய கோளகை) are obscure.

748.reading: The poet confesses that, not reckoning that life may slip in a moment, he took this life as lasting, and for the desires roused by women who receive any man, he went seeking gold, praising fools in the world as if each were Vishnu of the milk sea, and asks whether he must wander so. The praise names Murugan as the lord of the state reached by those who leave the six systems and still the mind, the son of the dancer to the beat, the bridegroom of the hunters' peacock girl, at Thiruvetkalam where the Vedas sound.
748.nuance: பார்க்களம் மீதினில் மூர்க்கரையே கவி பாற்கடலான் என: the poet's fault is flattering patrons as gods for gold; the gold is wanted for women (பாற்படு ஆடகம்). சாத்திரம் ஆறையும் நீத்த மனோலய சாத்தியர் sets the goal beyond all six philosophical systems.

links.note: Both confess the poet's trade of praising patrons in verse for gifts, likening men to gods (Vishnu of the milk sea here, clouds in giving in 15), and ask to be turned from it.
